reference.source: Williams Textbook of Endocrinology / Endocrine Society clinical guidance
clinicalPearls: A mosaic karyotype combining a 45,X line with a normal 46,XX line, generally producing a milder and more variable phenotype than classic monosomy X
Short stature and gonadal insufficiency remain the most consistent features, but their severity depends on the proportion of 45,X cells
Some individuals retain enough ovarian tissue for spontaneous puberty and even fertility, though premature ovarian insufficiency is common
Classic Turner stigmata such as webbed neck, lymphoedema, cardiac and renal anomalies occur less frequently than in non-mosaic disease
Because there is no Y-chromosome line, the gonadoblastoma risk that mandates gonadectomy in Y-bearing dysgenesis does not apply
Cardiac surveillance (particularly for bicuspid aortic valve and aortic dilatation) and renal, thyroid, hearing and metabolic monitoring remain important
Management includes growth optimisation, timely oestrogen replacement when ovarian function is insufficient, and fertility counselling
reference.pathophysiology: Turner syndrome mosaicism results from the coexistence of a 45,X cell line, usually arising from postzygotic loss of an X chromosome, alongside a normal 46,XX line. Haploinsufficiency of X-linked genes that escape inactivation, notably SHOX, contributes to short stature and skeletal features, while accelerated loss of oocytes leads to varying degrees of ovarian insufficiency. Because the phenotype reflects the tissue distribution and proportion of the 45,X line, presentations range from near-normal to features resembling classic Turner syndrome. The absence of any Y-bearing cell line means the streak-gonad tumour risk associated with Y material is not a concern in this karyotype.
additionalDifferentials: Noonan syndrome (phenotypic overlap with normal karyotype)
46,XX gonadal dysgenesis and premature ovarian insufficiency of other cause
Constitutional short stature or growth hormone deficiency
additionalInvestigations: Karyotype with adequate cell counts (and FISH where needed) to detect and quantify mosaicism
Serum gonadotropins and oestradiol to assess ovarian function
Echocardiography and, in adults, aortic imaging for cardiovascular anomalies
Thyroid function, glucose and lipid screening, and audiometry
Bone mineral density assessment and anti-mullerian hormone for fertility counselling
redFlags: Aortic root dilatation or bicuspid aortic valve raising the risk of dissection
Undiagnosed renal or cardiac structural anomaly
Untreated oestrogen deficiency leading to osteoporosis
Signs of autoimmune thyroid disease or impaired glucose tolerance
reference.prognosis: The prognosis is generally more favourable than in non-mosaic Turner syndrome, with a proportion achieving spontaneous puberty and occasionally fertility, though ovarian insufficiency and short stature are frequent. Long-term outcome depends on cardiovascular surveillance and management of associated endocrine and metabolic conditions.
pitfalls: Assuming a mild phenotype excludes cardiovascular and renal anomalies that still require screening
Overlooking premature ovarian insufficiency in someone who underwent spontaneous puberty
Applying the gonadectomy rule inappropriately when there is no Y-chromosome line
Insufficient karyotype sampling missing a low-level 45,X clone
references: International Turner syndrome clinical practice guidelines
management: Recombinant growth hormone to improve height where short stature is present
Oestrogen replacement to induce and maintain puberty followed by combined oestrogen-progesterone therapy, individualised because some retain ovarian function
Fertility counselling with consideration of oocyte cryopreservation given the risk of premature ovarian insufficiency, and assisted reproduction where needed
Cardiac surveillance for bicuspid aortic valve and aortic dilatation with echocardiography and aortic imaging
Monitoring for renal anomalies, thyroid disease, hearing loss, metabolic disturbance and bone health
No gonadectomy is required because there is no Y-chromosome line and hence no gonadoblastoma risk
Genetic counselling and multidisciplinary care coordinated across endocrinology, cardiology and clinical genetics
